ai_summary.headline: Gaza has a large MPC line but only 8% of it is funded, while WFP cash is being cut.
ai_summary.narrative: Gaza's cash response rests on a large MPC line: $592.6m of the $4.06bn flash appeal (14.6%), with 1.15m people in Gaza targeted for NIS 1,250 per round, in two cycles of three rounds [s1]. Funding is the constraint. FTS shows $46.4m received for MPC, about 8% of the requirement, against 36% for the plan overall [s2]. The Cash Working Group reports transfers set to the MEB value and roughly 100,000 households reached in February [s4][s5]. Sectoral cash appears to be rationed instead: WFP said in July it would keep full transfers for the most vulnerable and reduce them for others [s6], and in October it cut cash for 75,000 families [s7]. With 1.4m people acutely food insecure [s11] and Gaza need put at 2.1m [s1], targeting likely amounts to triage within near-universal need. We found no source saying WFP's transfer falls short of the MEB. Cited surveys show 75 to 84% prefer unrestricted cash [s1].
barriers: MPC only 8% funded against 36% for the plan
WFP cash cut for 75,000 families; transfers reduced for less vulnerable households (Oct 2026)
Near-universal need forces triage; MEB-level transfers cannot reach everyone
Crossing closures and thin non-food supply complicate modality choices
opportunities: Established CWG with a harmonised MEB-aligned transfer value and shared deduplication
Cash-out commissions fell to 12% by Dec 2025; pooled fund runs MPC projects
data_gaps: modality preference survey details and non-cash shares
sectoral cash and voucher requirements and funding

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: FTS single-cluster view of the Multi-purpose Cash Assistance cluster; shared-cluster view US$63.1M. Incoming flows, pledges excluded.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 64 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Protection US$15.0M, Food Security US$8.4M, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene US$3.6M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

cva_pct_of_total.note: cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

cva_to_local_pct.note: Indicator 4.2 proxy. Share of FTS cash funding (MPC cluster or CTP tag, US$85.3M) whose first-level recipient is a local or national NGO/CSO or a national government body. FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.

all_funding_to_local_pct.note: Share of all plan funding whose first-level recipient is a local or national actor (US$15.1M). Same first-level caveat.

cbpf_cva_to_local_pct.note: Second-level view: share of the pooled fund's cash grants (US$2.9M) that went to local or national actors. Pooled-fund grants are the one onward layer FTS records.

cbpf_all_to_local_pct.note: Share of all pooled-fund grants inside the plan (US$32.4M) to local or national actors.

localisation.caveat: FTS sees first-level recipients only; indicator 4.2 as defined (direct donor allocation to local partners) is therefore a floor. Chair roles come from public CWG pages and may be out of date.
